feedback: The final contradiction about woven tape makes a satisfying evidence-based accusation possible without needing a confession. I appreciated that several other guests continue lying: the player must distinguish an embarrassing lie from one about the murder mechanism. The six evidence pages are legible and the side-by-side photographs clarify the model and broken seal. Some captions do much of the interpretation, especially the repeated declarations that objects were real, uncovered or not substituted. That helps a large dinner group but reduces discovery. Voices differ through priorities: Monet thinks in payroll deadlines, Frank notices furniture even during distress, and Brie worries about staff and unpaid food. Repeated direct addresses to other characters give human connections, though virtually everyone delivers a neatly complete personal grievance on cue. Twenty-two speeches per act will be demanding in a noisy room. No attending-cast gap prevented my deduction, and the offstage technician, manager and coordinator have clear limited roles. The fair-play inference rests on combined evidence rather than a unique scrap match, which is explicitly and helpfully acknowledged.
